title: What is OSCER?
text:
The computational resource we will be using for this course will be the OU Supercomputing Center for Education and Research (OSCER).

Signing Up for an Account
Anyone on a project where the instructor or at least one Principal or Co-Principal Investigator is a faculty or staff member at an Oklahoma institution is elgible for an account.
Please visit the following link, it will take you to the page to sign up for an account: ACCOUNT SIGN UP
Follow step one and wait for confirmation of approval for your account before proceding to steps 2-3.
When asked to list a PI, if you are part of a lab please put your PI’s name. They will recieve and email about your account.


Changing Password
If you forget your password please visit the following link and follow the steps outlined: CHANGE PASSWORD


Template SBATCH Script
To submit jobs you must have the following lines at the start of the SBATCH script, no excpetion or it will not be submitted to the computer and will otherwise run on the login node. Running heavy jobs on the login node will get you noticed by the OSCER staff and you will recieve an email from Henry Neeman.
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --partition=normal
#SBATCH --ntasks=1
#SBATCH --mem=1G
#SBATCH --output=jobname_%J_stdout.txt
#SBATCH --error=jobname_%J_stderr.txt
#SBATCH --time=12:00:00
#SBATCH --job-name=jobname
#SBATCH --mail-user=youremailaddress@yourinstitution.edu
#SBATCH --mail-type=ALL
#SBATCH --chdir=/scratch/$USER

title: 16S rRNA Microbiome Analysis - Part 2
text:
6-Classifying ASV’s using a Feature Classifier
gg_version="gg_13_8_otus"
gg_ref_fasta="gg_ref/$gg_version/rep_set/99_otus.fasta"
gg_ref_tax="gg_ref/$gg_version/taxonomy/99_otu_taxonomy.txt"

primer_f="CCTACGGGAGGCAGCAG"
primer_r="GGACTACHVGGGTWTCTAAT"
region="v3_v4"

classifier_name="classifier-${region}-${gg_version}"
classifier_dir="output/5_classifier"

mkdir $classifier_dir

## Classifier Training
qiime tools import \
    --type 'FeatureData[Sequence]' \
    --input-path $gg_ref_fasta \
    --output-path $classifier_dir/${gg_version}-seqs.qza

qiime tools import \
    --type 'FeatureData[Taxonomy]' \
    --input-format HeaderlessTSVTaxonomyFormat \
    --input-path $gg_ref_tax \
    --output-path $classifier_dir/${gg_version}-taxonomy.qza

qiime feature-classifier extract-reads \
    --i-sequences $classifier_dir/${gg_version}-seqs.qza \
    --p-f-primer $primer_f \
    --p-r-primer $primer_r \
    --verbose \
    --o-reads $classifier_dir/ref-seqs-${region}.qza

qiime feature-classifier fit-classifier-naive-bayes \
    --i-reference-reads $classifier_dir/ref-seqs-${region}.qza \
    --i-reference-taxonomy $classifier_dir/${gg_version}_taxonomy.qza \
    --verbose \
    --o-classifier $classifier_dir/$classifier_name.qza
metadata_file="output/0_metadata_files/metadata-copy.tsv"
classifier="output/5_classifier/classifier_v3_v4_gg_13_8.qza"

tax_class_dir="output/6_taxa_classification"
mkdir $tax_class_dir

qiime feature-classifier classify-sklearn \
    --i-classifier $classifier \
    --i-reads $rep_seqs \
    --o-classification $class_sub_analysis_dir/taxonomy.qza
    
qiime metadata tabulate \
    --m-input-file $class_sub_analysis_dir/taxonomy.qza \
    --o-visualization $class_sub_analysis_dir/taxonomy.qzv

qiime taxa barplot \
    --i-table $rep_seqs_table \
    --i-taxonomy $class_sub_analysis_dir/taxonomy.qza \
    --m-metadata-file $metadata_file \
    --o-visualization $class_sub_analysis_dir/taxa-barplot.qzv

title: 16S rRNA Microbiome Analysis - Part 2
text:
8-Biomarkers with Picrust2
qiime feature-table filter-samples \
    --i-table $feat_table_file \
    --m-metadata-file $metadata_file \
    --o-filtered-table $picrust_dir/filt-freq-table.qza

qiime feature-table summarize \
    --i-table $picrust_dir/filt-freq-table.qza \
    --o-visualization $picrust_dir/filt-freq-table.qzv

qiime picrust2 full-pipeline \
    --i-table $picrust_dir/filt-freq-table.qza \
    --i-seq $rep_seqs_file \
    --output-dir $picrust_dir/full_pipeline \
    --p-placement-tool sepp \
    --p-threads $cores \
    --p-hsp-method pic \
    --p-max-nsti 2 \
    --verbose &> $picrust_dir/picrust2-fullpipeline.log 
for file in $picrust_dir/full_pipeline/*.qza;
do 
    file_name=$(echo $file | awk -F "/" '{print $4}' | awk -F "." '{print $1}')
    
    abundance_dir="$picrust_dir/full_pipeline/$file_name"
    mkdir $abundance_dir
    
    qiime feature-table summarize \
        --i-table $file \
        --o-visualization $abundance_dir/$file_name.qzv
        
    qiime tools export \
        --input-path $abundance_dir/$file_name.qzv \
        --output-path $abundance_dir/viz-$file_name
    
    qiime diversity core-metrics \
        --i-table $file \
        --p-sampling-depth $sampling_depth \
        --m-metadata-file $metadata_file \
        --output-dir $picrust_dir/full_pipeline/core-metrics-$file_name \
        --p-n-jobs $cores

done

title: 16S rRNA Microbiome Analysis - Part 1
text:
FULL SCRIPT
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --partition=ircfhp
#SBATCH --nodelist=c923
#SBATCH --container=el9hw
#SBATCH --nodes=1
#SBATCH --ntasks=1
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=10
#SBATCH --mem=30G
#SBATCH --chdir=/home
#SBATCH --output=qc_%A_%a_stdout.txt
#SBATCH --error=qc_%A_%a_stderr.txt
#SBATCH --mail-user=eleana-cabello@ouhsc.edu
#SBATCH --mail-type=ALL


#==============================================================================
# BASH Strict mode (i.e. "fail fast" to reduce hard-to-find bugs)
set -e          # EXIT the script if any command returns non-zero exit status.
set -E          # Make ERR trapping work inside functions too.
set -u          # Variables must be pre-defined before using them.
set -o pipefail # If a pipe fails, returns the error code for the failed pipe
                #  even if it isn't the last command in a series of pipes.
#==============================================================================

 module load QIIME2/2021.8

################################################
STEP 0
################################################
qiime_out_dir="output"
mkdir $qiime_out_dir

qiime metadata tabulate \
  --m-input-file sample-metadata.tsv \
  --o-visualization sample-metadata-viz.qzv

################################################
STEP 1
################################################
import_seqs_dir="output/1_imported_seqs"
manifest_file= ""

mkdir $import_seqs_dir

qiime tools import \
    --type 'SampleData[PairedEndSequencesWithQuality]' \
    --input-path $manifest_file \
    --input-format PairedEndFastqManifestPhred33V2 \
    --output-path $import_seqs_dir/demux-pairedend.qza

qiime demux summarize \
    --i-data $import_seqs_dir/demux-pairedend.qza \
    --o-visualization $import_seqs_dir/demux-pairedend.qzv
    
################################################
STEP 2
################################################
input_seqs="output/1_imported_seqs/demux-pairedend.qza"
f_primer=""
r_primer=""
error_rate=0.1
min_length=100
num_cores=22

trimmed_dir="output/2_trimmed_seqs"
mkdir $trimmed_dir

qiime cutadapt trim-paired \
    --i-demultiplexed-sequences $input_seqs \
    --p-cores $num_cores \
    --p-front-f $f_primer \
    --p-front-r $r_primer \
    --p-error-rate $error_rate \
    --p-minimum-length $min_length \
    --o-trimmed-sequences $trimmed_dir/trimmed-demux-pairedend.qza \
    --verbose \
  &> $trimmed_dir/trimmed.log 
  
qiime demux summarize \
    --i-data $trimmed_dir/trimmed-demux-pairedend.qza \
    --o-visualization $trimmed_dir/trimmed-demux-pairedend.qzv 

################################################
STEP 3
################################################

input_trimmed_seqs="output/2_trimmed_seqs/trimmed-demux-pairedend.qza"
num_cores=20
num_reads_learn=1000000
trunc_len_f=282
trunc_len_r=234

dada2_res_dir="output/3_denoised_seqs"
mkdir $dada2_res_dir

qiime dada2 denoise-paired \
    --i-demultiplexed-seqs $input_trimmed_seqs \
    --p-trunc-len-f $trunc_len_f \
    --p-trunc-len-r $trunc_len_r \
    --p-n-threads $num_cores \
    --p-n-reads-learn $num_reads_learn \
    --o-table $dada2_res_dir/feat-table.qza \
    --o-representative-sequences $dada2_res_dir/rep-seqs.qza \
    --o-denoising-stats $dada2_res_dir/denoising-stats.qza \
    --verbose \
    &> $dada2_res_dir/denoising_dada2.log 

qiime metadata tabulate \
    --m-input-file $dada2_res_dir/denoising-stats.qza \
    --o-visualization $dada2_res_dir/denoising-stats.qzv
    
qiime feature-table summarize \
    --i-table $dada2_res_dir/feat-table.qza \
    --o-visualization $dada2_res_dir/feat-table.qzv

qiime feature-table tabulate-seqs \
  --i-data  $dada2_res_dir/rep-seqs.qza \
  --o-visualization  $dada2_res_dir/rep-seqs.qzv

################################################

################################################

  --i-sequences $dada2_res_dir/rep-seqs.qza \

  --o-tree $phylo_tree_dir/unrooted-tree.qza \
  --o-rooted-tree $phylo_tree_dir/rooted-tree.qza

################################################
STEP 5
################################################

alpha_beta_dir="output/5_alpha_beta_div_rarefac"
mkdir $alpha_beta_dir

sampling_depth=""

qiime diversity core-metrics-phylogenetic \
  --i-phylogeny  $phylo_tree_dir/rooted-tree.qza \

title: Course Project
text:
Background
Throughout this summer course, we have primarily covered core data science concepts and how to perform a bulk RNA-seq analysis using the OUHC supercomputer. This experience has allowed you to become familiar not only with this specific type of analysis but also with important supporting skills such as working with bioinformatics software, understanding common bioinformatics file formats, and navigating the command line terminal. The purpose of this course project is to give you an opportunity to apply what you have learned over the past few weeks using either your own dataset or a dataset assigned to you.


Project Guidelines
Below is the general outline of the steps you need to take for this project:

Import data into your OSCER workspace, it can be your own, or we can assign data to you
Perform a quality check on your fastq files
Align your fastq read to the reference genome for your dataset using HISAT2
Produce a count matrix using the program featureCounts and the GFF file of your reference genome
Perform differential expression analysis using the R Bioconductor Package DeSeq2 and the count matrix you created in the previous steps



Submission
You will need to submit your presentation ahead of time on Canvas. Otherwise, everything else on the rubric you will need to cover in your presentation.
Please show the following during your presentation:

An organized OSCER workspace
An organized and annotated BASH script or scripts used to complete the project
R Workspace used to complete the analysis with dedicated folders and well-named files
A walkthrough of the Differential Expression Analysis Document with an explanation for each step

Comparing raw counts and normalized counts
Principal Components Analysis
Creation of DESeq2 Object using count matrix and sample metadata
Volcano Plot of results
Heatmap of results

Summary of key findings from the analysis
10 min limit, 5 slide limit

title: Programming in R for this Course
text:
Packages for this Course
We will be using R packages from both the Comprehensive R Archive Network (CRAN), the central repository for R packages, and Bioconductor, another repository that hosts thousands of packages specifically made for biomedical research.

CRAN Packages
Below is the code needed to install the CRAN packages needed for this course and import them into any script:
install.packages(c("tidyverse", "ggplot2", "pheatmap"))
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2) 
library(pheatmap)


Bioconductor Packages
Bioconductor packages work a little differently. First, the Bioconductor manager package BiocManager must be installed, and then using the methods of that package, you can install other Bioconductor packages like DESeq2:
if (!require("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE))
    install.packages("BiocManager")
    
BiocManager::install("DESeq2")
These packages can be imported into a script/workspace like typical CRAN packages after being installed through BiocManager:
library(DESeq2)

set -u          # Variables must be pre-defined before using them.
set -o pipefail  # If a pipe fails, returns the error code for the failed pipe
                #  even if it isn't the last command in a series of pipes.
#==============================================================================

echo "Hello World!" > helloWorld.txt
